title: Durga Ashtakam
intro: Durga Ashtakam is a hymn dedicated to Goddess Durga, invoking Her fierce and protective divine energy to overcome fears and adversaries.
description:
Namo namo durge sukh karani
Namo namo ambe duhkh harani।
Nirankar hai jyoti tumhari
Tihun lok phaili ujiyari।।

Shashi lalat mukh mahavishala
Netra lal bhrikuti vikarala।
Rup matu ko adhika suhave
Darash karat jan ati sukh pave।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

Tum sansara shakti lai kina
Palana hetu anna dhana dina।
Annapurna hui jag pala
Tum hi adi sundari bala।।

Pralayakala saba nashana hari
Tum gouri shiva shankar pyari।
Shiva yogi tumhare gun gaven
Brahma vishnu tumhen nita dhyaven।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

Rup sarasvati ka tum dhara
De subuddhi rishi munin ubara।
Dhara rupa narasimha ko amba
Prakata bhai phadakar khamba।।

Raksha kari prahlada bachayo
Hiranyaksha ko swarga pathayo।
Lakshmi rupa dharo jag mahin
Shri narayana anga samahin।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

Kshirasindhu mein karat vilasa
Dayasindhu dijai mana asha।
Hingalaja mein tumhi bhavani
Mahima amita na jata bakhani।।

Matangi dhumavati mata
Bhuvaneshvari bagala sukhadata।
Shri bhairava tara jaga tarini
Chhinna bhala bhava duhkh nivarini।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

Kehari vahana soha bhavani
Langura veera chalat agavani।
Kara mein khappara khadga viraje
Jako dekha kala dara bhage।।

Sohe kara astra aura trishula
Jate uthata shatru hiya shula।
Nagarkota mein tumhi virajata
Tihun loka mein danka bajata।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

Shumbha nishumbha danava tum mare
Raktabeeja shankhan sahare।
Mahishasura nripa ati abhimani
Jehi agh bhara mahi akulani।।

Rupa karala kalika dhara
Sainya sahita tum tihi sanhara।
Pari bhira santan para jaba jaba
Bhai sahay matu tum taba taba।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

Amarapuri aru basava loka
Taba mahima saba kahe ashoka।
Jwala mein hai jyoti tumhari
Tumhen sada pujen nara nari।।

Prema bhakti se jo yasha gave
Duhkh daridra nikata nahi ave।
Dhyave tumhen jo nara mana layi
Janma marana te so chuti jayi।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

Jogi sur muni kahata pukari
Yoga na ho bina shakti tumhari।
Shankara acharaja tapa kino
Kama aru krodha jiti saba lino।।

Nishidina dhyana dharo shankar ko
Kahu kala nahi sumiro tumko।
Shakti rupa ko marama na payo
Shakti gai taba mana pachatayo।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

Sharanagata hui kirti bakhani
Jaya jaya jaya jagadamba bhavani।
Bhai prasanna adi jagadamba
Dai shakti nahi kina vilamba।।

Moko matu kashta ati ghero
Tum bina kona harai duhkh mero।
Asha trishna nipata sataven
Ripu murakha mohe ati dara pave।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

Shatru nasha kijai maharani
Sumirou ikachita tumhen bhavani।
Karo kripa he matu dayala
Riddhi siddhi de karahu nihala।।

Jaba lagi jium daya phala paum
Tumharo yasha main sada sunaum।
Durga chalisa jo gavai
Saba sukha bhoga parama pada pavai।।

Devidasa sharana nija jani
Karahu kripa jagadamba bhavani।।
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)
(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

(Namo-namo, namo-namo)

faq.q1: Who is the author of Durga Chalisa?
faq.a1: According to the final verses of the hymn, Durga Chalisa was composed by Kavi Devidas, who sought refuge at the feet of Goddess Durga.
faq.q2: What are the benefits of reciting Durga Chalisa?
faq.a2: Regular recitation removes sorrows, poverty, and fear, protects against enemies, and grants the devotee wealth, peace, prosperity, and ultimate liberation (Moksha).
faq.q3: When is the best time and day to recite Durga Chalisa?
faq.a3: It is best recited early in the morning after daily ablutions. Chanting it during the festival of Navratri, as well as on Tuesdays and Fridays, is considered extremely auspicious.
faq.q4: Which forms of the Goddess are mentioned in Durga Chalisa?
faq.a4: Yes, alongside Goddess Durga, the hymn references various divine forms such as Mahakali, Annapurna, Saraswati, Lakshmi, Narasimha (protecting Prahlada), and several Mahavidyas (like Matangi, Dhumavati, Bagalamukhi, and Tara).
faq.q5: What is the significance of the repeating "(Namo-namo)" refrain?
faq.a5: It translates to "Salutations and bows again and again" to the Goddess. It enhances the devotional rhythm, energy, and absolute surrender to Mother Durga while chanting.
